title: Exact product-preserving inverse image transports the actual Koszul unit
statement: Let J and K be small sites and L a finite-limit-preserving left adjoint on their sheaves of sets, preserving countable products. Give L algebraic inverse-image data F as in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. For a commutative ring A and ideal I, suppose the canonical finite-projection completed coefficient map c:F(B_J)→B_K is an isomorphism, and countable products of modules over B_J and B_K are exact. For any finite list a of elements of A and any two strict Koszul limit presentations [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system] for their images, derived module pullback T along c admits a natural isomorphism Λ_J⋙T≅T⋙Λ_K carrying T of the actual Koszul unit to the actual target unit. No generation, Noetherian, or boundedness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, augmented finite Koszul tower; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 07A4 and 0941

proof.text: The invertible completed coefficient map identifies module pullback with pure inverse image. Its underlying-set comparison and the module adjunction make it additive, exact, and preserving countable products.

Apply canonical tensor pullback to the finite free factors. Their rank-one differential is multiplication by a_j^(m+1), and the dual transition is multiplication by a_j in degree -1 and identity in degree zero. Naturality of constants identifies these scalars and all quotient maps. Ordered tensoring identifies the strict dual Koszul tensor towers, naturally in an arbitrary complex, including their degree-zero augmentations.

Use exact products and exactProductFunctorStrictLimit for the normalized strict Roos comparison. On the signed shifted-cone coordinates it carries (gamma,0) to (F gamma,0). Descend the strict tower comparison and this normalized derived-limit comparison through localization. The tensor-factorization and right-derived universal properties identify the descended completion functors with the supplied presentations; their actual unit definitions give the required equation.

lean.statement:
theorem exactCompletedKoszulPullback
    {C D : Type v} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    {L : Sheaf J (Type v) ⥤ Sheaf K (Type v)}
    (F : InverseImageData L) (V : Sheaf K (Type v) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type v))
    (adj : L ⊣ V) [PreservesFiniteLimits L]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) L]
    (A : Type v) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    [IsIso (completedMap F A I)]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (Mod (completed J A I))]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (Mod (completed K A I))]
    (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A)
    (PX : KoszulPresentation J A I true r a)
    (PS : KoszulPresentation K A I true r a) :
    ∃ e : koszulCompletion J A I PX ⋙ (derivedPull F V adj (completedMap F A I)).functor ≅
        (derivedPull F V adj (completedMap F A I)).functor ⋙ koszulCompletion K A I PS,
      ∀ M, (derivedPull F V adj (completedMap F A I)).functor.map
          (koszulUnit J A I PX M) ≫ e.hom.app M =
        koszulUnit K A I PS ((derivedPull F V adj (completedMap F A I)).functor.obj M)
